mainEntity.name: How much does an Audi A6 50 TFSI e PHEV engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned or rebuilt Audi A6 50 TFSI e PHEV engine typically costs between £2,000 and £5,500 for supply only, depending on the specific engine code (e.g., DRYA or DLGA) and condition.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of water pump failure in an Audi A6 50 TFSI e PHEV?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early water pump or thermostat housing issues often present as persistent coolant loss without visible external leaks, or a sweet smell from the engine bay.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an Audi A6 50 TFSI e PHEV?

acceptedAnswer.text: For 2019-present models, the vehicle value typically ranges from £25,000 to £40,000. A full rebuilt engine (£3,200-£5,500) represents a small fraction of this value, making replacement a financially sound decision compared to scrapping.

mainEntity.name: How long does an Audi A6 50 TFSI e PHEV engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply and fit installation typically takes 8 to 11 hours of labour. Most independent specialists can complete the swap within 1 to 2 working days, assuming the replacement engine is readily available and high-voltage systems are safely isolated.

mainEntity.name: Can any garage fit an Audi A6 50 TFSI e PHEV replacement engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Because the 50 TFSI e is a plug-in hybrid, it contains high-voltage electrical systems. The fitting garage must have technicians certified in high-voltage vehicle repair, which our vetted network specialists possess.

problems.h4: Water Pump & Thermostat Housing Leaks - Why the Audi A6 50 TFSI e PHEV (DRYA / DLGA) Loses Coolant
problems.affectedModels: Audi A6 50 TFSI e PHEV (DRYA, DLGA, 2019-present)
problems.rootCause: The plastic composite water pump and thermostat housing is mounted on the rear of the engine. Heat cycling causes the plastic to warp or crack, leading to coolant loss.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replaces the water pump and thermostat housing assembly.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if caught early before overheating occurs.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded metal-composite components, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Required only if coolant loss led to severe overheating and cylinder head warping.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2019-present Audi A6 50 TFSI e PHEV is worth £25,000-£40,000 [THIRD-PARTY]. At this value, a £400-£800 component repair is highly viable, and even a full replacement (£3,200-£5,500) represents a small fraction of the vehicle's total value, making replacement financially safe.
problems.recommendation: Address coolant leaks immediately. If the engine has not overheated, a specialist water pump and housing replacement is the most cost-effective solution. Full replacement is only necessary if the cylinder head has been compromised by heat.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt DRYA Audi A6 50 TFSI e PHEV engine prices

problems.h4: Carbon Buildup & PCV System Issues - Why the Audi A6 50 TFSI e PHEV Runs Roughly
problems.affectedModels: Audi A6 50 TFSI e PHEV (DRYA, DLGA, 2019-present)
problems.rootCause: Direct injection combined with frequent short, electric-only trips means the intake valves are rarely washed by fuel, allowing carbon accumulation. The PCV valve can also degrade, causing oil consumption.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Walnut blasting carbon clean and PCV valve replacement.
repairOptions.longevity: Highly recommended as a preventative measure at 60k miles.
Only required if severe neglect led to valve damage or piston scoring.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2019-present Audi A6 50 TFSI e PHEV is worth £25,000-£40,000 [THIRD-PARTY]. A £300-£600 preventative clean is a minor investment that protects a high-value asset.
problems.recommendation: PHEV variants benefit greatly from regular combustion cycles to burn off deposits. If you primarily drive on electric power, schedule a preventative carbon clean and PCV check at 60,000 miles to avoid costly downstream damage.
